title: Pre-processing noisy production data using outlier detection methods reduces uncertainty in identifying flow regimes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Pre-processing noisy production data using outlier detection methods reduces uncertainty in identifying flow regimes
detail.abstract: This study presents machine learning-based outlier removal techniques as a pre-processing step for noisy production data (rate and pressure). Applying outlier detection (OD) methods helps reduce uncertainty in identifying flow regimes and preserves unique profiles of flow regimes. These methods are essential for addressing anomalies in production data and preventing inaccuracies in extracting reservoir properties.Flow regime identification involves constructing diagnostic tools such as a rate-normalized pressure (RNP) plot, commonly used in the rate-transient analysis (RTA). Our study simulated a synthetic log-log RNP profile from a fractured low-permeability gas reservoir and grouped the RNP data based on flow regimes. We added noise and outliers to the selected RNP data group in seven noise-presence scenarios using the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) technique with three levels of noise contamination and performed the OD process. We evaluated and analyzed twenty OD methods using performance metrics, such as mean absolute error (MAE), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score.The F1 score combines precision and recall metrics to assess the effectiveness of OD methods. While one method can accurately detect outliers in one situation but inaccurately in another, the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) consistently outperforms others, maintaining an average F1 score of 0.9. Optimal input parameters for GMM are a threshold factor of 0.8 to 1.1 and a component number of 7 to 10. We performed sensitivity calculations for these input parameters in the case of field data. In the synthetic case, GMM produces a cleaner RNP profile, achieving an impressive accuracy of 93.99%.This work expanded previous studies of OD methods on RNP data by evaluating twenty methods across various noisy data scenarios based on flow regimes. Our findings highlight robust OD methods, reducing subjectivity and time consumption while improving the precision of flow-regime profiles for more accurate production forecasts and EUR predictions.

title: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have become a dominant vehicle in equity investing, yet their growing scale also raises concerns about how shocks are transmitted across increasingly overlapping market segments

detail.title: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have become a dominant vehicle in equity investing, yet their growing scale also raises concerns about how shocks are transmitted across increasingly overlapping market segments
detail.abstract: This study examines the dynamic connectedness structure of 25 major U.S.-listed equity ETFs covering broad-market, growth, size, value/dividend, sector, international developed, and emerging-market exposures. Using daily data from February 2016 to February 2026, the analysis applies a time-varying connectedness framework based on an adaptive vector autoregressive specification and generalized forecast error variance decomposition. The empirical design is complemented by descriptive return diagnostics, regime-wise analysis, rolling-correlation assessment, and network visualization.,The results show that the equity ETF universe is highly interconnected, with a large share of return variation explained by cross-ETF spillovers rather than fund-specific disturbances. Broad-market ETFs consistently occupy central positions in the network and act as net transmitters of shocks, whereas several sectoral and internationally oriented ETFs more often behave as net receivers. Connectedness intensifies during periods of market stress, particularly during the COVID-19 episode, when diversification benefits weaken substantially and category correlations with the U.S. benchmark rise sharply. Network evidence further indicates that crisis periods are associated with a more concentrated transmission structure centred on a smaller set of dominant benchmark funds.,These findings suggest that equity ETFs should be viewed not only as passive diversification instruments but also as channels of systemic transmission within the broader financial system. The study contributes to the literature by examining a broad cross-category ETF network, linking connectedness with diversification performance across regimes.

title: Integrated multiscale modeling and coordinated balance-of-plant optimization to maximize vehicle system efficiency in a heavy-duty fuel cell electric vehicle
affiliations: Seoul National University, Seoul National University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Seoul National University and Seoul National University

detail.title: Integrated multiscale modeling and coordinated balance-of-plant optimization to maximize vehicle system efficiency in a heavy-duty fuel cell electric vehicle
detail.abstract: This study presents an integrated multiscale modeling and optimization framework for polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems in a heavy-duty fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV). The influence of balance-of-plant (BoP) operation on parasitic power consumption and vehicle system efficiency was quantitatively investigated. The integrated model combined the air supply system, thermal management system (TMS), and a quasi-three-dimensional stack model to capture the coupled electrochemical and thermal behavior under realistic operating conditions. The air supply system was validated using component-level experimental data, while the TMS was validated via full-scale chassis dynamometer tests. The model accurately reproduced transient responses, including temperature and pressure, with coefficients of determination (R2) exceeding 0.95. Vehicle-level analysis identified the radiator hydraulic fan pump as the dominant contributor to parasitic losses across the entire operating range. To maximize stack voltage and vehicle system efficiency, the coordinated BoP control parameters were optimized using a Box-Behnken design, Pareto analysis, and response surface methodology under a thermal constraint on the stack coolant outlet temperature. At the maximum stack load of 95 kW, the fan pump consumed 17.18 kW, while the air compressor and coolant pump consumed 12.45 kW and 0.80 kW per stack, respectively. Under the coordinated BoP strategy, the stack voltage and vehicle system efficiency improved by 1.88 and 4.03 %, respectively, demonstrating that coordinated BoP control effectively reduces parasitic losses under high-load conditions. The proposed framework provides a validated foundation for system-level BoP optimization and supports the development of high-efficiency control strategies in commercial heavy-duty FCEVs.

title: From Liberalisation to Penalisation:  Structural Origins of the Motherhood Penalty under China's Two-Child Policy

detail.title: From Liberalisation to Penalisation:  Structural Origins of the Motherhood Penalty under China's Two-Child Policy
detail.abstract: Following China’s 2016 Two-Child Policy, mothers’ employment income declined sharply and female labour force participation fell. This paper identifies a supplyside mechanism rooted in employment-contingent maternity benefits. We develop a dynamic search model with sequential fertility decisions in which employment at parity one acquires option value as a platform for accessing future paid maternity leave. This induces one-child mothers to lower reservation wages, generating an endogenous wage penalty through self-selection into lower-quality matches. The model generates sharply heterogeneous responses by parity: one-child mothers return to work more quickly, trading wage quality for employment speed, while childless women become marginally more selective. Fertility increases through both extensive and intensive margins but remains well short of doubling. Comparative statics reveal strong non-linearities: the option-value mechanism strengthens when maternity benefits are generous but collapses when childrearing costs are high or labour-market prospects for mothers are weak. These results show how motherhood penalties can arise endogenously from social insurance design and why fertility liberalisation alone may have limited labour-market effects.
